claim: LLM-simulated wargame teams reproduce coarse human patterns but not individual action frequencies: statistical match on 16/21 (GPT-3.5), 10/21 (GPT-4), 9/21 (GPT-4o) actions against 214 experts in 48 teams; newer models matched fewer actions.
agent_test: Run our simulate-a-plan step on a task with a human baseline; report share of outcomes that match baseline; compare at equal tokens against a single no-simulation answer.

claim: Simulated runs are better for comparing conditions (plan A vs B) than for absolute prediction: treatment-effect significance mostly agreed with humans (China posture agreed; AI accuracy null in all) but crew training differed for GPT-4/4o.
agent_test: On items with known plan rankings, check whether simulated A-vs-B ordering matches truth more often than simulated absolute scores match truth.

claim: Simulated team dialog inside one model gives fake agreement (short statements, rarely disagree), shifts aggressiveness and action count, and does not add independent opposition. Replication on full GSM8K: debate gain is no larger than majority vote at equal responses.
agent_test: Compare one-call decision vs same-model multi-role dialog on the plan-test step at equal tokens; count disagreements raised and final accuracy.

claim: Persona prompts are an unreliable lever: vague background and extreme pacifist/sociopath labels had no significant effect (Lamparth, menu game, 3 models), while goal-stating hawk/dove personas changed armed conflict 1/20, 4/20, 14/20 (Snow Globe, one 7B model).
agent_test: Vary adversary persona text (background vs explicit goals) and measure outcome shift; keep only goal-stating roles.

claim: All tested LLM nation agents escalated in simulated wargames and none showed significant de-escalation; levels differ strongly by model (GPT-4-Base nuclear 6.7-7.1% of actions vs 0-0.21% for chat models).
agent_test: Run the same scenario on the model we use; log escalation score per step; flag drift in code.

claim: Escalation drift is an artefact movable by sampling and prompt: on Mistral-7B, temperature 1.0 to 0.5 cut escalation 38%, to 0.01 cut 48%, planning reflection cut 28%, de-escalation reflection cut 57% (10 runs each); Rivera's own eight prompt variants mostly did not matter.
agent_test: Run our simulated opponent at two temperatures and with/without a reflection slot; check whether plan verdicts change.

claim: Free-form LLM crisis answers are semantically inconsistent across 20 samples for all five models; meaning-preserving rewording at T=0 gives inconsistency comparable to T=0.2, so T=0 does not make a simulated judge stable.
agent_test: Run the plan-test step N=5 times with paraphrased prompts; report spread; require agreement before accepting a verdict.

claim: Single wargame runs are heavy-tailed: escalation spikes of over 50% in one turn in GPT-3.5/GPT-4 runs; one run is not evidence.
agent_test: Compare verdict from 1 run vs median of k runs at equal total tokens.

claim: Generate-then-run with a real simulator score works: COA-GPT beat RL baselines on mean reward with no training (50 rollouts per variant), best vision+feedback variant 3.4% below one human expert (15 trials); human feedback raised mean and cut variance.
agent_test: On a task with an executable checker, compare propose-run-revise against propose-once at equal tokens.

claim: A staged domain-structured prompt multiplied win rate vs built-in StarCraft AI (L3 25% to 100%, L4 12.5% to 84%, L5 0 to 50%, L6 0 to 8.3%), with gains largest where the plain prompt had a foothold.
agent_test: Plain vs staged prompt at equal tokens across graded difficulty; test whether gain shrinks at the hardest tier.

claim: Same-model opposing sides are not independent adversaries: one scripted defector exploits LLM Diplomacy players, frontier models in nuclear-crisis play never chose any of eight de-escalatory options in 21 games/329 turns, and Richelieu's self-play gain over Cicero was not significant.
agent_test: Replace an LLM adversary with a code-built or different-model adversary and compare number of plan flaws found.

claim: Behaviour and verdicts are framing dependent: deadline framing flipped win rates (Claude 100% to 33%, GPT-5.2 0% to 75%); adding a middle option or swapping actor names changed model choices (CFPD); actor country shifted escalation recommendations.
agent_test: Score a plan under 3 framings and anonymised actors; flag verdicts that flip.

claim: Historical-match tests are confounded by recall: de-anonymised WWI runs hit 97.43% alliance and 100% mobilisation accuracy, while war broke out in every run even after counterfactual fine-tuning; an outcome that never moves with facts is bias, not skill.
agent_test: Change one key fact in a scenario; require the simulated outcome to change; otherwise discard the simulator verdict.

claim: Written reasoning from simulated agents is not a reliable record of cause: stated signals matched later actions only about 70% of the time; justifications for nuclear use appear in chain-of-thought.
agent_test: Compare stated plan vs executed action in the simulated run; score by code, not by narrative.

claim: Almost no research tests an LLM that both plays and adjudicates: 20 of 223 papers (9%) give LMs both roles; LLM adjudicator validity is untested, and known faults are repeated output and drift from stated plans.
agent_test: Check adjudicated outcome against stated plan by code; measure drift rate for code vs LLM adjudication.

claim: For exact tactical search, code beats LLM play: all LLMs scored NRA -1 against MCTS in complete-information deterministic games though they beat random agents.
agent_test: On a checkable sub-problem, compare LLM judgment vs code search at equal tokens.

claim: Automated plan generation plus wargaming can match staff quality at far lower effort: CADET 4.2 vs human 4.4 (9 judges, 20 packages), about 0.4 vs 16 person-hours; judge scatter large (SD about 2).
agent_test: Use many raters or code checks; do not rely on one grader.

claim: Machine players escalating more than humans is an old claim (RAND 1950s) but its base is thin: Emery describes a formal math game (nuclear early) versus a free-play game that never went nuclear; the computer-causes-nuclear-use reading is second-hand.
agent_test: Not directly testable; avoid citing as hard evidence.

claim: Selecting by measured outcome beats using all attempts: fine-tuning on wins from the top 25% by utilisation gave 54/100 vs 28/100 win rate.
agent_test: Pick best of N by code-computed score vs random sample at equal tokens.

claim: Cranfield/AIAA studies named in the subfield row were not opened; no numbers exist for them. Gap search: repository entry found, scores plans by mission success and asset survivability; full text blocked (403), still no numbers.
agent_test: None until read.

claim: Revision from the same model's own critique does not raise accuracy and often lowers it; revision helps only with an external executable or ground-truth signal. So a simulate-then-revise step needs a real simulator, not a self-critique.
agent_test: Arms at equal calls: (a) no revision, (b) revise from own critique, (c) revise from a code or rules check. Score each against ground truth; expect c above a, b at or below a.

claim: More samples of a verdict help a lot only when the check is exact (code, proof): coverage rises log-linearly (SWE-bench Lite 15.9% to 56% at 250 samples). Without an exact check, majority vote and reward models plateau (MATH 40.50% to 41.41% from 100 to 10,000 samples). Adaptive allocation by difficulty beats fixed best-of-N by over 4x efficiency.
agent_test: For plan verdicts, vary k in 1, 3, 5, 10 at equal token budget and measure verdict stability and accuracy; look for the plateau.

claim: LLM judges agree with humans over 80% on chat preferences but carry position, verbosity and self-enhancement bias; no study validates an LLM adjudicator against a human adjudicator on wargame plan outcomes.
agent_test: Have a model and a human adjudicate the same simulated turns; measure agreement, with answer order swapped and a different-family judge.

claim: Persona prompts do not add factual accuracy (162 personas, 2,410 questions, no gain; best persona per question about as good as random) and explain under 10% of annotation variance, but help where the persona carries information about the target response. Consistent with null for background personas and effect for goal-stating ones.
agent_test: Compare goal-stating vs background persona on a simulated actor across two model families; score behaviour change and plan accuracy separately.

claim: Adversary diversity: a code/RL-built exploiter beat LLM Diplomacy agents (Welfare Diplomacy), and a mix of three model families in debate scored 91% vs 82% for three copies on GSM-8K. Neither test used an equal-call vote baseline, so the size of the diversity effect is not settled.
agent_test: Red-team a plan with (a) same model, (b) other family, (c) rule or code adversary, at equal tokens; count real flaws found against a seeded-flaw plan.
